title: Distributed systems & messaging patterns
literature: POSA1 & POSA4 (distributed-object, broker, proxy); Hohpe & Woolf EIP (channels, routing, transformation, endpoints); Coulouris/Tanenbaum distributed systems; each pattern realizes/refines a style and relates to sibling patterns.

members.name: API Composition
members.what: A composer queries multiple services and joins their results in memory to answer a query that spans service-owned databases.

members.name: Authoritative Server
members.what: One server owns the true game/simulation state; clients send inputs and locally predict, then reconcile against authoritative snapshots.

members.name: Bodyguard
members.what: Shares objects across address spaces without full RPC by attaching a guard that intercepts and validates operations on the shared object.

members.name: Client Proxy (remoting)
members.what: A local object presenting the remote component's interface inside the client process, forwarding invocations to the remoting machinery.

members.name: Client Request Handler
members.what: Client-side middleware component that manages network resources, sends request messages and receives replies for requestors.

members.name: Competing Consumers (system topology)
members.what: Multiple independently deployed consumer instances pull from one shared message channel, so load spreads and any instance's failure is absorbed by the rest.

members.name: CQRS
members.what: The system's write model (commands) and read model (queries) are separated into distinct models, often with distinct stores kept in sync asynchronously.

members.name: Crash-Only Software
members.what: A system is structured so its components have exactly one stop method (crash) and one start method (recover), making crash-restart the universal, well-tested recovery path.

members.name: Data Bus (RTDP)
members.what: A system-wide shared bus abstraction through which components publish and read common data instead of holding pairwise links.

members.name: Database per Service
members.what: Each service exclusively owns its persistent data; other services access it only through the service's API.

members.name: Datatype Channel
members.what: The channel topology is organized so each channel carries messages of exactly one data type, letting receivers know a message's type from the channel it arrived on.

members.name: Demilitarized Zone
members.what: Externally reachable services are placed in a separate network segment between two firewall layers, isolating them from both the internet and the internal network.

members.name: Distributed Hash Table
members.what: Nodes form a self-organizing overlay in which consistent-hashing-based routing locates the node responsible for any key in O(log n) hops.

members.name: Distributed Snapshot
members.what: Marker messages flow through a distributed system's channels so each node records a mutually consistent cut of global state without stopping the world.

members.name: Domain Object (POSA4)
members.what: Encapsulates each distinct unit of application functionality as a self-contained component behind an explicit interface, as the root partitioning move of a distributed design.

members.name: Durable Subscriber
members.what: The messaging infrastructure persists a subscriber's subscription so that messages published while the subscriber is disconnected are saved and delivered when it reconnects.

members.name: Event-Carried State Transfer
members.what: Events carry the full changed state so consumers maintain local replicas and need not call back to the source system.

members.name: Event Collaboration
members.what: Components collaborate by broadcasting events about what happened rather than requesting each other to act, each maintaining its own state from the stream.

members.name: Fault Containment Region
members.what: A set of components (typically a node computer) engineered so that the immediate consequences of an internal fault stay inside the region's boundary, which is defined and enforced architecturally.

members.name: Fault-Tolerant Unit
members.what: A group of replica-deterministic fault containment regions that produce the same outputs so that the failure of a member is masked by the remaining replicas (duplex fail-silent or triplicated voting configurations).

members.name: Firewall
members.what: A barrier that restricts access to designated resources (typically processors, memory, and network connections); a specific realization of the security Limit Access tactic used to keep unsafe effects from propagating.

members.name: Guaranteed Delivery
members.what: The messaging system persists every message to a local data store at each hop before acknowledging, and deletes it only after successful handoff to the next store, so messages survive crashes and outages end to end.

members.name: Half-Object plus Protocol (distribution structure)
members.what: Splits one logical object into coordinated halves in two address spaces with a private protocol keeping them consistent.

members.name: Invoker
members.what: Server-side middleware component that receives invocations, unmarshals them and dispatches to the target remote object's method.

members.name: Kernel-Bypass Networking
members.what: Restructures the I/O path so the application drives the NIC from user space via polled queues, bypassing the kernel network stack.

members.name: Leader Election
members.what: Cooperating instances select exactly one of themselves as coordinator for a role, and re-elect when the leader fails.

members.name: Leaderless Replication
members.what: Clients (or coordinators) write to and read from multiple replicas directly, using read/write quorums, read repair, and hinted handoff instead of a leader.

members.name: Message Broker
members.what: A central intermediary receives messages from all senders and routes (and often transforms) them to the appropriate receivers, so every application couples only to the hub.

members.name: Message Endpoint
members.what: The component that connects an application to a messaging channel, encapsulating send/receive mechanics at the application boundary.

members.name: Message Router
members.what: A component that consumes messages from one channel and republishes them to different channels according to routing conditions.

members.name: Multi-Leader Replication
members.what: Several nodes accept writes concurrently and asynchronously replicate to each other, requiring conflict resolution.

members.name: Object Synchronizer
members.what: Decouples object replicas' synchronization policy from their functionality, coordinating state updates between distributed replicas.

members.name: Policy Decision Point / Policy Enforcement Point
members.what: Authorization is externalized: enforcement points embedded at resource boundaries defer every access decision to a central policy decision point that evaluates declarative policy.

members.name: Preforked / Prethreaded Server
members.what: The server creates a pool of processes or threads at startup that take turns accepting and serving connections.

members.name: Presentation-Abstraction-Control
members.what: Structures an interactive system as a hierarchy of cooperating agents, each with its own presentation, abstraction, and control facet, communicating only through the control facets.

members.name: Primary-Replica Replication
members.what: One node accepts all writes and streams its change log to replicas, which serve reads and can be promoted on failure.

members.name: Process Pairs
members.what: A primary process executes while a backup process on another node receives checkpoints and takes over transparently when the primary fails.

members.name: Proxy-Based Firewall
members.what: A firewall that terminates connections and re-issues them via per-protocol proxies, inspecting traffic at application level.

members.name: Reflection
members.what: Splits a system into a base level doing the application work and a meta level holding a self-representation (metaobjects) whose modification changes the base level's behavior and structure at runtime.

members.name: Remote Facade
members.what: A coarse-grained facade over fine-grained objects provides the remote interface, bundling many small interactions into few large calls.

members.name: Replicated Component Group
members.what: Deploys a component as a coordinated group of replicas presented as one logical component, for availability or load distribution.

members.name: Requestor
members.what: Client-side middleware component that constructs and sends remote invocations on behalf of proxies, handling marshaling and result delivery.

members.name: Server Request Handler
members.what: Server-side middleware component that accepts connections, receives request messages and hands them to invokers, returning replies.

members.name: Sharding
members.what: A dataset is split by key across nodes (range or hash partitioning) so each shard is stored and served independently, with rebalancing and request routing.

members.name: Thread-per-Connection Server
members.what: The server dedicates a freshly created process or thread to each accepted connection for its lifetime.

members.name: Two-Phase Commit
members.what: A coordinator drives distributed atomic commit: participants first vote prepared, then all commit or all abort on the coordinator's decision.
